items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: George Treadwell, who was Sarah Vaughan's husband, called me and asked me if I would come with Sarah as her accompanist.

ctx.x: him off and on, whenever he had a job. If he had three or four weeks, he would call me, and I would come, and then after that I would come to Washington and play a gig here and there. Somebody would call me to go out for a couple of days or something.

But the last I worked with him, we played a job in Birdland. While we were in Birdland... It was just before the turn of the year from '51 to '52. George Treadwell, who was Sarah Vaughan's husband, called me and asked me if I would come with Sarah as her accompanist. Jimmy Jones, the pianist that had been with her, was very ill and was in the hospital for an operation, and the situation was such as they thought that he would be there for quite some time. So I told him I would think about it.

Then I asked him, 'Well, just how long do you think?' -- because he said quite some time, and I thought he meant about two or three weeks, or something like that. So he made a statement, and one that I think nobody should ever make. He said, 'Jimmy Jones is not coming back at all.' I said, 'Why?' He said Jimmy had lung cancer, and they were going to take out a lung or something like that, and he says, 'To tell you the truth, Jimmy Jones is going to die, and if you want the job, it's yours.'
